arguments.note: Reviewed release_disk_guard.py + test_release_disk_guard.py standalone (not yet wired into old publisher). SHA256: release_disk_guard.py=9ff152103eee99f229d2c16fa785d8b02690a4885c955bf1620c6d0bfd195aec; test_release_disk_guard.py=689aada7c6b95292ec0d7d07d83e35c635c47d0c4e8f94d0024f324427e23f77. Ran `python -m unittest test_release_disk_guard -v` locally: 3/3 tests pass (healthy_headroom, old_four_gigabyte_guard_is_insufficient, pressure_not_ready_missing_and_taint). validate() correctly requires Ready=True, DiskPressure=False, and absence of node.kubernetes.io/disk-pressure taint per node, raising AssertionError (not swallowed) on any node missing/failing a condition or on empty node list. Headroom guard is max(total//5, 4_000_000_000) i.e. 20% of disk or 4GB floor, a real improvement over the old flat 4GB-only check (test proves 5GB avail on 100GB total now fails where old guard would pass). __main__ block correctly calls GET https://quiz.kotopedia.org/health/ready and asserts status==200 and empty body. Gap: only validate() has unit coverage; the live kubectl/disk_usage/urllib wiring in __main__ is exercised only via disk-recovery/ evidence, not unit tests. Cross-checked disk-recovery/ evidence: disk-guard-live.txt + disk-guard-live-exit.json show actual guard run exiting 1 with AssertionError: Insufficient disk headroom, matching recovery-status.json (guard_actual_exit=1, status=BASELINE_RESTORED_CANDIDATE_NOT_PUBLISHED). feedback-after-restore.json shows all 29 feedback rows status=open, matching recovery-status.json's all_29_feedback_preserved_open=true -- consistent, no discrepancy found. baseline-restore-exit.json, owned-disk-recovery-exit.json, owned-docker-tag-recovery-exit.json all show actual_exit=0, consistent with a clean rollback to helm revision 57. LIMITATIONS (must be stated, not glossed over): this guard is a point-in-time check only -- it cannot guarantee against concurrent disk consumption by other processes/pods between the check and the actual image pull/write, and its 20%/4GB thresholds are a hardcoded assumption, not read from the node's actual kubelet --eviction-hard/--eviction-soft imagefs.available config, so it will mismatch any cluster with non-default kubelet thresholds. This review covers the script quality only. Per recovery-status.json, historical publication approval54 is obsolete after recovery57; this review does NOT approve publication, and the guard is not yet integrated into the old publisher.
